key_insight: The paper presents a unified analytical loss model that explains and compares performance limits in photoelectrochemical cells by decomposing losses and linking them directly to design choices.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a practical way to diagnose bottlenecks in PEC devices and prioritize optimizations such as better catalysts, nanostructuring, or improved semiconductor-electrolyte matching.
method: Applies one physically consistent framework to both built-in junction and semiconductor-electrolyte junction photoelectrodes.
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency metrics, and efficiency maps under ideal and real conditions.
Fits experimental JV data to separate thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial losses, then visualizes energy flow with Sankey diagrams.
evidence_signal: The framework was validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, including comparisons among Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: The model is only as reliable as the quality of the fitted experimental data and its simplifying physical assumptions, so device-specific effects may still require additional validation.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
